page: Amazon Web Services r7a.32xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by the AMD EPYC 9R14 processor family using the x86_64 architecture, providing 128 dedicated physical cores and 128 vCPUs with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration running at 3.7 GHz. The system provides 1024.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 5 GHz, equating to 8.0 GB of memory per core, alongside 32 MB of L3 cache per complex.

The instance configuration includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions for disk operations and persistence. Hardware accelerator options are not present, with zero discrete GPUs. Network performance is provisioned with a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps, accommodating high-throughput data replication and node synchronization without relying on complimentary public IPv4 allocations.

Benchmark evaluations reflect top-tier ratings across both compute and memory-intensive evaluations. The server logged a multi-core stress-ng metric of 392562.57 and a PassMark CPU score of 128997.72. Memory subsystem throughput measured 565.57 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 311.25 GB/sec for large-block writes. Redis SET benchmarks registered 246.48 million operations per second, while LLM prompt processing reached 360.52 tokens per second on a 7B model.

Given its high memory capacity and 1:8 core-to-memory ratio backed by 128 non-hyperthreaded physical cores, the r7a.32xlarge delivers resource efficiency for workloads requiring strict thread isolation and massive RAM residency. Primary workload fits include enterprise in-memory databases, large Redis or Memcached clusters, big data transformation, software compilation, and data analytics.
